evidence.claim: Built to protect stages and settlers against Cheyenne and Sioux raids, the fort had accommodations for 500 men, with troops dispersed between Fort Hays and Fort Denver.
evidence.quote: Fort Wallace (c. 1865–1882) was a US Cavalry fort built in Wallace County, Kansas to help defend settlers against Cheyenne and Sioux raids and protect the stages.

evidence.claim: Little Jerusalem’s chalk formed 85 million years ago beneath the Western Interior Seaway.
evidence.quote: Niobrara chalk formations in Little Jerusalem Badlands State Park were formed 85 million years ago, when the area was covered by the Western Interior Seaway.

evidence.claim: Fossils found here include swimming and flying reptiles, giant clams and oysters.
evidence.quote: the remains of swimming and flying reptiles dating back 85 million years have been found here. Ancient giant clams and oysters are common fossils in these badlands.

evidence.claim: The chalk also supports living habitat: Great Plains wild buckwheat grows in western Kansas chalk-bluff prairie and nowhere else in the world.
evidence.quote: This native plant is found in the chalk bluffs prairie of western Kansas and nowhere else in the world.
